sub: Named after al-muddaththir, “the one wrapped in a cloak”, in ayah 1
theme: The Prophet ﷺ is commanded to rise and warn. The surah then answers the man who called the Qurʾan magic: Saqar awaits the deniers, and the Qurʾan is a reminder for whoever wills.
story: Revealed in Makkah. Its opening ayat are among the very first. After the first revelation in the cave of Ḥirāʾ, revelation paused. Then the Prophet ﷺ saw the same angel seated between sky and earth, hurried home shaken, and said, “Wrap me up.” Ayat 1–5 came then.

From then on, revelation came strong and steady. The rest of the surah came later, after public preaching began. Quraysh’s chiefs wanted one charge to spread among the Hajj pilgrims, and al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, after long thought, called the Qurʾan magic.

The surah describes him without naming him: his wealth, his scowl and his verdict. Then it shows Saqar, who ends up there and why, and why people run from the reminder. Their plan backfired: it spread the Prophet’s name across Arabia.

sections.title: Arise and warn
sections.meaning: The Prophet ﷺ, wrapped in his cloak, is told to get up and warn, declare his Lord’s greatness, keep his clothes and himself pure, shun idols, give without seeking more, and be patient for Allah. Then the warning itself: when the trumpet sounds, that Day is hard for the disbelievers.
points: You wrapped in a cloak: arise and warn
Glorify your Lord, purify your clothes, keep away from idols
Don’t give to get more; be patient for your Lord
When the trumpet sounds: a hard Day for the disbelievers
sections.matters: These are among the first commands of the Prophet’s mission. Before he warns anyone, he is shaped: glorify Allah, stay pure, give without expecting a return, and be patient. Then comes the message he must carry: a hard Day is coming.
sections.story: After a pause in revelation, the Prophet ﷺ saw the angel of Ḥirāʾ between sky and earth, rushed home and asked to be wrapped up; ayat 1–5 came. Another report says he wrapped himself in grief after Quraysh called him a magician.
explained: Al-muddaththir is someone wrapped in a dithār, a thick outer cloak: a gentle way of calling him. Qum: get up and warn. Declare your Lord’s greatness. Purify your thiyāb: your actual clothes, and also your heart, deeds and character. Keep away from ar-rujz: idols, or all sin.

Walā tamnun tastakthir: don’t give hoping to get more back, or don’t count your favours as great. Be patient for your Lord through the hardship ahead. Then the warning: when an-nāqūr, the trumpet, is blown, that Day is severe and not easy for the disbelievers, which implies it is easier for believers.
teaches: The caller to Allah starts with himself: clean clothes, clean heart, clean deeds.
Proclaim Allah’s greatness above everything people magnify.
Do good without expecting anything back from people.
Calling to the truth brings hardship; bear it for Allah.
sections.hook: Ayat 2–7 are short commands, most ending fa- + verb: fa-andhir, fa-kabbir, fa-ṭahhir, fa-hjur, fa-ṣbir. Ayah 6 is the one “don’t”. Rabbaka (3) and li-rabbika (7) frame the list.

sections.title: The man who called it magic
sections.meaning: Leave Me with the man I created alone, then gave wealth, sons at his side and an easy life, yet he wants more. No: he fought Our signs. He thought, frowned, turned away in pride, and called the Qurʾan magic and human speech. So he will burn in Saqar, guarded by nineteen.
points: Created alone, given wealth, sons and ease, yet wants more
No! He fought Our signs; a crushing climb awaits
He thought and plotted; destroyed be he, how he plotted!
Looked, frowned, turned away: “just magic, just human words”
Into Saqar: it spares nothing and scorches the skin
Over it are nineteen
sections.matters: It shows what happens when pride blocks a truth someone already recognises. This man admitted the Qurʾan was not poetry, madness or soothsaying, yet called it magic to keep his standing. His blessings only made him want more.
sections.story: Revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, a rich Quraysh chief. He heard the Qurʾan and admitted its beauty. Pushed by Abū Jahl to say something against it, he thought, scowled, and called it magic that splits a man from his father, brother and wife.
explained: Dharnī: leave him to Me. Allah created him alone, with no wealth or children, then gave him wide wealth, banīn shuhūdā (sons always at his side), and an easy life. Still he hoped for more. Kallā: he was ʿanīd, stubbornly opposing signs he knew were true. So he will be forced up ṣaʿūd, a crushing climb.

Then his decision in slow motion: he thought, weighed his words, looked, frowned, scowled, turned his back in pride, and said: “Only magic handed down; only the words of a man.” Twice he is cursed for it. His end is Saqar, which leaves nothing unburned and scorches the skin, with nineteen angels over it.
teaches: Knowing the truth is not enough if pride blocks it.
Worldly blessings are no sign you will do well in the Hereafter.
Don’t twist the truth to protect your status.
Be grateful for what you have instead of demanding more.
sections.hook: Thumma, “then”, opens ayat 20, 21, 22 and 23: his decision in slow motion. Qaddar ends 18, 19 and 20. Page 576 begins at ayah 19.

sections.title: Nineteen: a test and a warning
sections.meaning: The keepers of the Fire are angels, and their number was given as a test. It makes the People of the Scripture certain and believers firmer, while doubters ask what it means. Only Allah knows His armies. By the moon, night and dawn: the Fire is one of the greatest things, a warning to all.
points: Angel keepers; the number tests some and strengthens others
No! By the moon, the leaving night, the brightening dawn
The Fire is one of the greatest things, a warning
For whoever wills to step forward or hang back
sections.matters: It answers the mockery about nineteen and teaches how to receive the unseen: accept what Allah tells you. The same news raises one person’s faith and another’s doubt. Then the oath makes the warning certain, and leaves the choice to each person.
sections.story: When ayah 30 was heard, Abū Jahl mocked: couldn’t every ten of Quraysh overpower one of them? A Quraysh strongman boasted he would take on seventeen if they took two. Ayah 31 answered: the keepers are angels, and none knows Allah’s armies but Him.
explained: The disbelievers imagined fighting Hell’s keepers. But they are angels, stern and immensely strong. Their number is a fitnah, a test: the People of the Scripture find it matches what they have and become certain, believers grow in faith, and the doubters and disbelievers ask, “What does Allah mean by this?”

So the same words guide some and leave others astray. Nineteen are not all His soldiers: only Allah knows how many He has. Kallā: by the moon, the night as it leaves, and the dawn as it lights up, Saqar is one of the greatest calamities, a warning to whoever wills to step forward or fall behind.
teaches: Accept the unseen as Allah describes it; don’t split hairs over it.
The same revelation can raise faith or deepen doubt.
Allah’s armies are beyond anyone’s count.
Each person chooses: step forward to faith or fall behind.
sections.hook: Ayah 31 is by far the longest ayah of the surah, surrounded by short ones. The oaths follow a night’s order: moon, night leaving, dawn breaking (32–34).

sections.title: What put you into Saqar?
sections.meaning: Every soul is held in pledge for what it earned, except the people of the right. From their gardens they ask the criminals what brought them into Saqar. The criminals confess: we didn’t pray, didn’t feed the poor, joined in empty talk, and denied the Day until death came. No intercession helps them.
points: Every soul held for its deeds, except the people of the right
In gardens they ask: what put you into Saqar?
We did not pray, nor feed the poor
We joined vain talk and denied the Day until death
No intercessor’s plea will help them
sections.matters: In the criminals’ own words, it lists what leads to Saqar: neglecting prayer, neglecting the poor, plunging into falsehood with others, and denying the Day. The confession comes too late for them, but not for the person reciting it today.
sections.story: No specific incident. It continues the picture of Saqar by showing who ends up there and why.
explained: Rahīnah: every soul is held like a pledge, bound by the wrong it earned. The people of the right, the believers given their record in the right hand, go free. In their gardens they ask about the criminals, then ask them: mā salakakum fī saqar, what brought you into Saqar?

Their answer is a confession. We were not among al-muṣallīn, we did not feed the miskīn, we plunged into falsehood with those who plunged, and we denied the Day of Recompense until al-yaqīn, death, came. For people like this no intercessor’s plea helps: intercession benefits only those Allah is pleased with.
teaches: Prayer is Allah’s right; feeding the poor is people’s right. Neglect neither.
The company you keep and the talk you join can drag you down.
Deeds count only until death arrives.
Intercession will not help someone who died denying the Day.
sections.hook: The confession has a pattern: lam naku, “we were not” (43, 44), then kunnā, “we used to” (45, 46), then ḥattā, “until” (47). Page 577 begins at ayah 48.

sections.title: Running from the reminder
sections.meaning: Why do they turn from the reminder, running like startled wild donkeys fleeing a lion? Each of them wants his own scripture delivered to him. No: they simply don’t fear the Hereafter. The Qurʾan is a reminder; whoever wills will take heed, yet only if Allah wills. He deserves to be feared, and He forgives.
points: Why turn away, like wild donkeys fleeing a lion?
Each wants his own scroll; really, they don’t fear the Hereafter
No! It is a reminder; whoever wills will remember
Only if Allah wills; He deserves fear and grants forgiveness
sections.matters: It names the real reason people run from the Qurʾan: not a lack of proof but no fear of the Hereafter. And it ends the surah with hope: the One who deserves to be feared is also the One who forgives.
sections.story: Quraysh’s disbelievers reportedly demanded that each of them wake up to find a scroll from Allah by his head, ordering him to follow the Prophet ﷺ. Ayah 52 exposes that demand, and ayah 53 gives the real reason behind it.
explained: At-tadhkirah, the reminder, is the Qurʾan. They bolt from it like ḥumur mustanfirah, panicked wild donkeys fleeing a qaswarah: a lion, or hunters. Then they make grand demands: each wants ṣuḥuf munashsharah, open scrolls sent to him personally. Kallā. The real problem is that they don’t fear the Hereafter.

Kallā: this is a reminder, and whoever wills will take it to heart. Yet no one takes heed unless Allah wills: people truly choose, and their choice stays within His will. He is ahl at-taqwā, the One who deserves to be feared, and ahl al-maghfirah, the One who forgives whoever fears Him.
teaches: Running from reminders comes from not fearing the Hereafter.
Demanding special proof is often an excuse, not a search.
You truly choose, and your choice stays within Allah’s will.
Fear Allah, and never lose hope in His forgiveness.
sections.hook: The root dh-k-r runs through the ending: tadhkirah (49, 54), dhakarahu (55), yadhkurūn (56). Kallā opens both 53 and 54. The surah closes on a pair: ahl at-taqwā, ahl al-maghfirah.

groups.text: You wrapped in your cloak, get up and warn people.
Declare your Lord’s greatness, purify your clothes and yourself, and keep away from idols and sin.
Don’t give hoping to receive more, and be patient for the sake of your Lord.
When the trumpet is blown, that Day will be hard, and not at all easy, for the disbelievers.
Leave Me with the man I created alone, then gave wealth, sons and comfort. Still he wants more.
No! He stubbornly opposed Our signs, so he will be forced up a crushing climb.
He thought and weighed what to say against the Qurʾan. Destroyed be he, how he weighed it!
He looked, frowned, turned away in pride, and said: it is only magic handed down, only human words.
He will burn in Saqar, which spares nothing and scorches the skin. Nineteen guard it.
The keepers are angels. Their number tests the disbelievers and strengthens believers, and only Allah knows His armies.
No! By the moon, by the night as it leaves, by the dawn as it brightens.
The Fire is one of the greatest things, a warning to everyone, whether they step forward or hang back.
Every soul is held for what it earned, except the people of the right.
In gardens, they ask the criminals: what brought you into Saqar?
“We did not pray, and we did not feed the poor.”
“We joined in empty talk and denied the Day of Recompense, until death came to us.”
No intercessor’s plea will help them.
Why do they turn from the reminder, like wild donkeys fleeing a lion?
Each wants his own scrolls sent down. No: they just don’t fear the Hereafter.
The Qurʾan is a reminder for whoever wills, but only if Allah wills. He deserves fear, and He forgives.

1.explain: Al-muddaththir: the one wrapped in a dithār, a thick outer cloak. Calling the Prophet ﷺ by the state he was in is a gentle, affectionate way to address him.
1.why: After a pause in revelation, the Prophet ﷺ saw the angel from Ḥirāʾ seated between sky and earth. Shaken, he went home saying “Wrap me up,” and ayat 1–5 came. Another report: he wrapped himself in grief after Quraysh called him a magician.

2.explain: Qum fa-andhir: get up with energy and warn people of what awaits them if they don’t believe. With this command he was sent out as a messenger.

3.explain: Wa rabbaka fa-kabbir: declare your Lord’s greatness, in word and action, above every idol people set up beside Him.

4.explain: Wa thiyābaka fa-ṭahhir: keep your clothes clean of impurity. It also means purify your heart, intentions, deeds and character, and don’t wear what was earned unlawfully.

5.explain: Ar-rujz: idols, or all sin. Keep away from it. He ﷺ never worshipped idols; the command is to stay away from them for good.

6.explain: Walā tamnun tastakthir: don’t give something hoping to get more back. Or: don’t remind people of your favours and count them great.

7.explain: Wa li-rabbika fa-ṣbir: be patient for your Lord’s sake, with people’s harm, in obeying Him and in avoiding what He forbids. Calling people to Allah will bring hardship.

8.explain: Nuqira fin-nāqūr: when the trumpet, a horn, is blown to raise everyone from their graves.

9.explain: That Day will be ʿasīr: severe and hard, because of its many terrors.

10.explain: Not easy for the disbelievers, who have lost all hope of good. The wording implies it will be easy for the believers.

11.explain: Dharnī: leave him to Me. Allah created him waḥīd, alone in his mother’s womb, with no wealth and no children.
11.why: Revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, a Quraysh chief. He praised the Qurʾan as unlike any human speech, then, stung by Abū Jahl’s taunts, called it magic from long ago.

12.explain: Māl mamdūd: wide, ever-growing wealth from crops, herds and trade.

13.explain: Banīn shuhūdā: sons always present with him. They didn’t need to travel for trade, so he enjoyed their company. Reportedly ten, or seven, three of whom later accepted Islam.

14.explain: Mahhadtu lahu tamhīdā: I smoothed everything for him: wealth, status and a long, comfortable life.

15.explain: Still he hopes I will give him more: more wealth and children, or even the blessings of the Hereafter, as he got those of this world.

16.explain: Kallā: no more. He was ʿanīd, stubborn against Our signs: he recognised them and still fought them. Reportedly his wealth and children kept shrinking after this until he died.

17.explain: Saʾurhiquhu ṣaʿūdā: I will force him up a crushing climb, either a mountain of fire in Hell or a torment with no relief.

18.explain: Innahu fakkara wa qaddara: he thought hard about what to say against the Qurʾan, and settled on a line in his mind.
18.why: Quraysh’s chiefs wanted one charge to spread about the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Walīd rejected “soothsayer”, “madman”, “poet” and “sorcerer” as unbelievable. After long thought he said: call him a magician whose words split a man from his father, brother and wife.

19.explain: Fa-qutila kayfa qaddar: may he be destroyed, how he plotted! A curse, full of amazement at such a scheme against Allah’s words.

20.explain: Thumma qutila kayfa qaddar: repeated for emphasis. Destroyed again, how he plotted!

21.explain: Thumma naẓar: then he looked, either at his people’s faces or for something to attack the Qurʾan with.

22.explain: Thumma ʿabasa wa basar: then he frowned, and scowled even harder, his face showing his dislike of the truth.

23.explain: Thumma adbara wastakbar: then he turned his back on faith and was too proud to follow the Prophet ﷺ.

24.explain: Siḥrun yuʾthar: “This is only magic, handed down from the magicians of old.”

25.explain: “This is only the words of a human being,” not the words of Allah. He claimed the Prophet ﷺ had picked it up from others.

26.explain: Saʾuṣlīhi saqar: I will burn him in Saqar, a name of Hell, surrounding him on every side.

27.explain: Wa mā adrāka mā saqar: what will make you realise what Saqar is? The question shows how terrible it is.

28.explain: Lā tubqī wa lā tadhar: it leaves nothing, not flesh or sinew, unburned. Then they are made anew for more, neither living nor dying.

29.explain: Lawwāḥatun lil-bashar: it scorches the skin and turns it black.

30.explain: ʿAlayhā tisʿata ʿashar: nineteen angels are in charge of it, stern and strong.

31.explain: The keepers are angels, not men anyone could overpower. The number nineteen is a test: believers accept it, doubters mock it. And nineteen are not all: only Allah knows how many soldiers He has.
31.why: When ayah 30 came, Abū Jahl mocked: can’t every ten of you overpower one of them? A Quraysh strongman boasted he would handle seventeen if they handled two. This ayah answered them: they are angels.

32.explain: Kallā: either “no!” to the mockers, or “truly”. Then an oath by the moon, one of Allah’s great signs.

33.explain: …and by the night as it withdraws.

34.explain: …and by the morning as it brightens. Moon, night and dawn all point to Allah’s power and wisdom.

35.explain: Innahā la-iḥdā al-kubar: Saqar is one of the greatest calamities.

36.explain: Nadhīran lil-bashar: it stands as a warning to all humanity.

37.explain: For whoever wills to step forward to faith and obedience, or to hang back in sin. The warning reaches everyone; each one chooses.

38.explain: Rahīnah: every soul is held in pledge, bound by the wrong it earned, like an item held until a debt is paid.

39.explain: Except aṣḥāb al-yamīn, the people of the right: the believers who receive their record in the right hand. They are not held; they go free.

40.explain: In gardens, at ease with everything they wished for, they ask one another…

41.explain: …about the criminals, and look in on them in Hell.

42.explain: “Mā salakakum fī saqar? What put you into Saqar? Which sin earned it?”

43.explain: “We were not among al-muṣallīn, those who prayed.” They did not worship Allah.

44.explain: “And we did not feed the miskīn.” They did no good to people in need.

45.explain: “We plunged into falsehood with those who plunged”: talking about what they didn’t know, and going astray with whoever went astray.

46.explain: “And we denied the Day of Recompense,” the Day of judgement and reward. It grew out of all that empty talk.

47.explain: “Until al-yaqīn came to us”: the certainty, meaning death. After that, every chance was gone.

48.explain: Intercession helps only those Allah approves of. Someone who died denying the Day gets nothing from any intercessor, however many. Believers who sinned can still benefit.

49.explain: At-tadhkirah: the reminder of the Qurʾan. What is wrong with them, turning away from it?

50.explain: Ḥumur mustanfirah: wild donkeys in a panic, each startling the others into running faster.

51.explain: Fleeing a qaswarah: a lion, or hunters. That is how they bolt when they hear the Qurʾan.

52.explain: Each wants ṣuḥuf munashsharah, open scrolls sent to him personally. Reportedly they demanded to wake up with a letter from Allah by their heads telling them to follow the Prophet ﷺ.

53.explain: Kallā: they won’t get it. The real reason is that they don’t fear the Hereafter. If they did, they wouldn’t make such demands.

54.explain: Kallā: truly, this Qurʾan is a tadhkirah, a reminder.

55.explain: So whoever wills will remember it and take the lesson. The way has been made clear.

56.explain: Yet no one remembers unless Allah wills: people truly choose, within His will. Ahl at-taqwā: He deserves to be feared. Ahl al-maghfirah: He forgives whoever fears Him.
